question.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3x) \\  & =x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3) \\  & =1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
